newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African bank workers to protest armed robberies.
newsitem.headline: S.African bank workers to protest armed robberies.

text.p: Leading banks in several South African cities are expected to shut down on Thursday when around 50,000 employees protest against a wave of armed robberies sweeping the country, a union official said.

"This issue (bank robberies) is so serious that it has actually mobilised our members. We expect 50,000 to participate in protest marches," Ben Venter, spokesman for the South African Society of Bank Officials (SASBO), told Reuters on Monday.
"Basically we are protesting against violence, crime and bank robberies. We want action from the government against this situation," he said.
The protests are expected to stretch over two hours, starting at noon.

Venter said main branches of leading banking groups Standard Bank Investment Corp Ltd, First National Bank, Nedcor and Absa will close during the two hour-long noon protest action in Cape Town, Johannesburg, Durban, Pretoria and Port Elizabeth
But smaller branches will remain open, he said.
Bank employers represented by the Council of South African Banks (COSAB) have given the protest action their full support, a COSAB official said.
Venter said about 164 violent armed robberies had taken place around the country so far this year in which many members had been hurt or killed.
"Something must be done against organised crime. Gangsters must be removed from society," he said.
Since President Nelson Mandela won the country's first all-race elections in 1994, political violence has dropped dramatically but criminal violence has soared.
Police figures show 1.8 million crimes were reported in South Africa last year and South African banks estimate that robberies cost the industry some $25 million a year.
